title: Umar's death
hook: stabbed at dawn prayer, he names a council of six to choose his successor

segments.voice: Yesterday, the plague, and a caravan that turned back from God's decree to God's decree. Your line was: don't enter, don't leave. What step did you take for your health? Day eight hundred seventy-six.

Dawn in the mosque at Medina. The rows are forming. Umar walks between them as he used to before the prayer, telling people to straighten their lines. He takes his place at the front and says God is greatest. And in that moment a man steps out of the dark and stabs him. A man named Amr ibn Maymun was standing in the rows, and Bukhari keeps what he saw. Today: Umar's death.
screen: `DAWN, AND THE ROWS FORMING.` → `GOD IS GREATEST.` → `A MAN STEPS OUT OF THE DARK.`

segments.voice: Umar falls, and the first thing he does is reach for Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's hand and pull him forward to lead the prayer. The prayer goes on, short and quiet. Afterward Umar asks who struck him. A slave of al-Mughirah, he's told. And Umar says: praise be to God, who did not let my death come at the hands of a man who claims Islam. They bring him milk to drink, and it comes out of the wound, and the people around him understand. A young man comes in and praises him: your companionship with the Prophet, your justice. Umar answers: I wish it would come out even, nothing against me and nothing for me. Then he sends his son Abdullah to Aisha, with a request: may Umar be buried beside his two companions? She says she had wanted the place for herself, but she will give it to him. And then the question everyone is waiting for. Who leads next? Umar does not name a son. He does not name one man. He names six, the companions with whom, he says, the Prophet was pleased when he died: Ali, Uthman, al-Zubayr, Talhah, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman. Let them choose one from among themselves. His own son may sit with them, but have no share in the choice. The Qur'an praises those whose affairs are settled by consultation among them. Umar made his last act a consultation. Sunni Muslims honor this council as the way Uthman was chosen; Shia Muslims, as with the succession, read these events differently. The council itself is tomorrow's story.
screen: `HE PULLS ABD AL-RAHMAN FORWARD.` · `NOT BY ONE WHO CLAIMS ISLAM.` · `BURIED BESIDE HIS TWO COMPANIONS.` · `SIX NAMED. NO SON, NO HEIR.` · then, large: `A COUNCIL, NOT A CROWN.`

segments.voice: The practice: the dawn prayer. If you pray, you might set an alarm and pray fajr tomorrow, at the hour Umar was standing in the rows. If you don't, you might simply wake a little early tomorrow and sit for a minute at first light. For now, close your eyes if you like. Picture the mosque before sunrise, the rows straight, the quiet. Breathe in, and think of a man who, wounded, made sure the prayer continued. Breathe out. Decide on your dawn. The bell holds the time.
Umar's death. Stabbed as he began the dawn prayer, he had the prayer go on, asked to be buried beside his two companions, and named six to choose from among themselves. Today's word.
Your line: a council, not a crown. Today, before you decide something that affects others, ask them first. Day eight hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: Muslims retell Umar's death from the long report in Sahih al-Bukhari, and the council he named is taught in Sunni history as the shura that chose Uthman; his grave lies beside the Prophet's and Abu Bakr's in Medina.

fork.setup: you're Umar, dying. the people ask who will lead after you. what do you do?
options: name the one man you think is best.
name six, and let them choose one among themselves.
fork.reveal: he named six companions with whom the Prophet was pleased, and gave his own son no share in the choice.

original.note: Arabic: consultation, the word used for the council Umar named.

trapdoor: what you thought: a ruler dies and his heir takes over.
what it means: dying, Umar named no heir. he named six to choose one among themselves.
what a scholar hears: Amr ibn Maymun's eyewitness report in Bukhari, the shura of six, and a council Sunni and Shia Muslims read differently.

notes: Bukhari 3700 cited from memory; confirm the number and every detail paraphrased (the rows, Abd al-Rahman leading, the attacker as al-Mughirah's slave, the milk, 'nothing against me and nothing for me', Aisha's permission, the six and Abdullah's role).
The attacker, Abu Lu'lu'ah, is not named; the script says 'a man who was not a Muslim' following Umar's words in the report. Confirm the phrasing is fair and fits Bukhari.
Bukhari's report also gives numbers of others stabbed; left out.
Sunni and Shia readings of the shura mentioned without ranking; confirm.
Qur'an 42:38 paraphrased; Pickthall's wording not quoted to avoid error.
Editor pass: Amr ibn Maymun no longer called 'the companion'; he lived in the Prophet's time but is counted among the generation after, not a sahabi. Confirm.
